title: Three reports, one placement count

metrics.reason: One of the three counts being compared. The GATE is `parity_violations`: what matters is that the three agree, not what number they agree on. A floor here would fail every run where the cohort legitimately changed size.
Same — reported separately only so a parity failure names WHICH report moved.
Same. The fixture's `expectPlacements` already pins the cohort's own count, and a drift there is reported as a parity violation.

notes: In-process over the synthetic cohort — no database. Runs the three real computations (computeGrantKpis, buildDohsExportRows, computeFunnel) over one population and asserts they agree on how many people got a job. Each count is also reported on its own so a failure says WHICH report moved. The three self-directed applications in the cohort are deliberately non-qualifying, so the funnel's comparison line is non-zero while the three placement counts still agree — a fixture where they qualified would make the reports legitimately disagree and turn this into a test of the fixture.
